newsitem.title: USA: Men less ready to relocate for spouse's career - study.
newsitem.headline: Men less ready to relocate for spouse's career - study.

text.p: When it comes to relocating for a spouse's career, men are less willing than women to pull up stakes, according to a study released Tuesday by Allied Van Lines, the largest U.S. moving company.

Forty percent of men, versus 70 percent of women, said they would be willing to move if their spouse or significant other were relocated to another geographic area for job reasons, said Naperville, Ill.-based Allied.
The findings were based on a survey in March and April of 1,000 Americans done by Opinion Research Co., Allied said.
The study found that 34 percent of men said they would refuse to move if their spouse were relocated for job reasons, but only 14 percent of women took the same stance.

"While the survey results underscore men's reluctance to move, their attitudes will likely change. Fifteen percent of all transferees are now women, and as women continue to advance into executive positions, that number is expected to grow," said Allied Chief Executive Mike Fergus.
